title: The complete input profile of a group of 3D bridges: what Part 1 writes and Part 2 reads

s.description: Metres from the first end of the chain

z_m.description: The height of the point above the ground, 0 or more (with z_reference elevation: its elevation)

curve_m.description: The length of the vertical curve around the point, in metres (0: none). The filler writes it; the maker needs it

source.description: Where the value comes from: data, rule, given, example, a survey...

id.description: The ground id: the SHA-256 of the elevation file (duckOSM main.elevation_metadata.sha256)

curve.description: smooth: the curve of today. design: straight grades and vertical curves

height_rule.description: How the filler finds a height that was not given. length: today's rule. design: the design rules

z_reference.description: What z_m is. ground: metres above the ground of the page (the default; a free end is 0). elevation: the elevation in the vertical datum of the profile's ground (every node needs one)

id.description: The id of the node in a complete profile

lonlat.description: The position of the node. In a partial input it names the node: the node of the group within 5 m

kind.description: ground: one chain ends here, height 0. junction: chains meet here

portal.description: A free end where the deck goes straight into a tunnel (a road of level below 0 starts at the node). The engine writes it; with z_reference elevation the page does not check the ground there

chains.description: The chains that meet at the node

z_m.description: The height of the node above the ground, in metres, 0 or more (with z_reference elevation: its elevation in the datum of the ground, any number)

source.description: Where the value comes from: data, rule, given, example, a survey...

osm_ways.description: The OSM ways of the chain, when the roads have them. In a partial input they name the chain

from.description: The node at the first end of the chain

to.description: The node at the last end of the chain

points.description: Interior control points, in order of s (the curve design)

top_m.description: The full height of the chain: the height that its ramps are made for (the curve smooth). The page's __rs_full. Above 0 (with z_reference elevation: the highest elevation of the chain)

width_m.description: The width of the deck, in metres. Without it, each road is drawn at the width of its class
